headline: XDOF raises $70M to build data pipelines for AI robotics
summary: The startup is creating the essential data infrastructure that AI labs need to teach robots how to interact with the physical world.
details: The race to build capable robots is on, but a critical bottleneck has emerged: the lack of high-quality training data. Unlike language models trained on vast text datasets, robots require data that captures physical interaction, which is scarce. XDOF is emerging to address this gap by building the necessary data pipelines, collection tools, and annotation systems.

XDOF has secured $70 million in funding from prominent investors including Thrive Capital, Spark Capital, a16z, Lux, and WndrCo. The company, with around 60 employees, is already collaborating with 20 customers, including several leading AI labs, though specific names remain confidential.

CEO Philippe Wu highlighted the urgency, stating that major AI labs are heavily investing in robotics. He emphasized the need to avoid falling behind in this new frontier, drawing parallels to the early stages of the language model race.

The company's origins trace back to Wu's PhD research at UC Berkeley, where he encountered the 'chicken-and-egg' problem of needing data to train foundation models for robotics. This led to the development of GELLO, a teleoperation system that generated influential research in data collection for robotics.

XDOF is partnering with UC Berkeley's AI Research lab to release ABC, what they claim is the largest collection of high-quality robot training data ever assembled. This dataset includes 130,000 robot manipulation trajectories, 300 hours of simulation, and 100 hours of evaluations.

This extensive pre-training data, previously unavailable to academia, is expected to accelerate community-driven advancements in robotics, similar to how open data has spurred progress in language and image generation fields. The team has already used this data to train robots for tasks like folding laundry and packing items.

XDOF plans to operate on a three-tiered data pyramid. The most valuable data comes from teleoperation on the actual robot, followed by general data collected via teleoperated robots, and finally 'egocentric' data from human tasks, for which XDOF will develop its own wearable sensors.

XDOF is stepping in with $70M to build it.

topic: sixty percent of US consumers say 'AI' in brand messaging is a turnoff
headline_marked: [[60% of US consumers]] say 'AI' in brand messaging is a turnoff
headline: 60% of US consumers say 'AI' in brand messaging is a turnoff
summary: A new report reveals that a significant majority of consumers find AI mentions in marketing to be a negative signal, suggesting a growing distrust in AI-driven brand communication.
details: A recent survey indicates that 60% of US consumers view the inclusion of 'AI' in brand messaging negatively.
This sentiment suggests a growing skepticism and potential distrust towards artificial intelligence in marketing and brand communication.
The findings also point to a broader feeling that the internet has become less human over the past decade, with AI potentially contributing to this perception.
As brands increasingly integrate AI into their services and marketing, this consumer reaction highlights a critical challenge in balancing technological advancement with human connection.
caption:
Is 'AI' in brand messaging a turnoff? A new report says 60% of US consumers think so.

A recent survey indicates that 60% of US consumers view the inclusion of 'AI' in brand messaging negatively.

This sentiment suggests a growing skepticism and potential distrust towards artificial intelligence in marketing and brand communication.

The findings also point to a broader feeling that the internet has become less human over the past decade, with AI potentially contributing to this perception.

As brands increasingly integrate AI into their services and marketing, this consumer reaction highlights a critical challenge in balancing technological advancement with human connection.
